title: When Audio-Language Models Fail to Leverage Multimodal Context for Dysarthric Speech Recognition
reasoning: The paper primarily investigates the performance of audio-language models on dysarthric speech recognition. While the conclusion contains a small subsection on ethical implications regarding clinical labeling and potential social biases, the core research and benchmarking focus on Word Error Rate (WER) and technical model adaptation rather than evaluating or benchmarking religious, moral, or ethical frameworks.
